[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This document is a step-by-step guide for product engineering teams adopting a Golden Path for a service or repository. It covers what you need in place before you start, how to set up a repository, the warning-only pilot sequence, how to move to fail-hard enforcement, how runtime monitoring is activated post-deployment, and how to keep a repository current as the catalog evolves.

This document describes what teams do. The catalog governance process (how paths are authored, reviewed, and published) is documented in PTN-GOV-AI-001.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#who-this-is-for]

### Who This Is For

**Primary:** Engineers and team leads onboarding a new or existing service to a published Golden Path.

**Secondary:** Platform Engineering members guiding teams through onboarding. Architects reviewing repositories for ARB submissions.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#scope]

### Scope

This guidance covers:
- New repositories starting from a Golden Path scaffold
- Existing repositories adopting a Golden Path retroactively
- Repositories using AI coding agents (GitHub Copilot, autonomous pipelines)
- Catalog version updates for repositories already on a path

This guidance does not cover:
- Authoring a new Golden Path — see [GUID-GOV-PROC-004 Golden Path Authoring Playbook](GUID-GOV-PROC-004-golden-path-authoring-playbook.md) for the end-to-end component sequencing, inter-component dependencies, and ARB submission assembly
- The exception process when a gate fails — see [GUID-GOV-PROC-002 Exception Management Process](GUID-GOV-PROC-002-exception-management-process.md)
- Runtime monitor invariant authoring — see PTN-APP-GOV-003

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#prerequisites-before-any-team-can-adopt]

## Prerequisites Before Any Team Can Adopt

Platform Engineering must complete these steps before the first team onboards to a path. If any of these are missing, stop and contact `#platform-engineering`.

| Prerequisite | Pattern | Check |
|---|---|---|
| At least one Golden Path published in the catalog with a machine-readable index entry | PTN-GOV-AI-001 | Does `platform.gainwell.internal/golden-paths` return a valid entry for your path ID? |
| Verification Contract exists for the path | PTN-GOV-AI-003 | Does `catalog/verification-contracts/[path-id]-verification-contract.yaml` exist in the catalog repository? |
| Compliance Evidence Store operational | PTN-GOV-AI-004 | Does the evidence store accept pipeline artifacts? Test with a dry run from a sandbox pipeline. |
| Architecture Fitness Suite deployed for the path | PTN-APP-GOV-001 | Is the fitness suite co-located with the path in the catalog repository? |
| AI Governance Policy published | PTN-GOV-AI-002 | Is `ai-governance-policy.yaml` published in the EA Reference Architecture repository and referenced in path context files? |
| Exception management process defined and published | PTN-INFRA-GOV-001 | Is [GUID-GOV-PROC-002](GUID-GOV-PROC-002-exception-management-process.md) published? Gate must not run in fail-hard mode until this is true. |
| ARB charter updated to include Golden Path review as a standing agenda item | PTN-GOV-AI-001 | Has the ARB confirmed a 2-week review cycle for path-related submissions? |

The exception management process prerequisite is non-negotiable: **the conformance gate must not be set to fail-hard mode until GUID-GOV-PROC-002 is published and the ARB triage SLA is in place.** Teams blocked with no recourse will find their own workarounds (PTN-INFRA-GOV-002: *"Exception process must exist before enforcement is enabled; teams blocked with no recourse route around the gate"*).

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#step-11--declare-the-golden-path-in-serviceyaml]

### Step 1.1 — Declare the Golden Path in `service.yaml`

Add the `golden_path` field to the repository's root `service.yaml` (or `catalog-info.yaml`). This is the declaration the Architecture Conformance Gate reads to identify which Verification Contract to load (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, Phase 2 Step 2).

```yaml
# service.yaml (repository root)
service:
  name: eligibility-api
  team: benefits-platform
  golden_path: HIPAA-REST-MICROSERVICE-AKS-V1
  compliance_scope:
    - HIPAA
    - FedRAMP-Moderate
  environment: production
```

The `golden_path` value must match the path ID in the machine-readable catalog index exactly. If the path does not exist in the index, the gate reports `unknown-path` and blocks. Verify the path ID against the Developer Portal before committing.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#step-12--set-up-ai-context-files]

### Step 1.2 — Set Up AI Context Files

Create the `.ai/` directory and populate the required context files. These files configure AI coding agents (GitHub Copilot, autonomous pipelines) to generate output that conforms to the Golden Path (PTN-APP-GOV-002).

Use the **Context File Requirement Decision Guide** below to determine which files are mandatory for your repository type:

| Repository Type | `.ai/context.yaml` | `.ai/constraints.md` | `.ai/instructions.md` | `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HIPAA-scoped microservice (GP-001) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** (autonomous pipeline) / optional (developer-only) |
| FedRAMP-scoped microservice (GP-007) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** |
| Shared library (no Golden Path) | Recommended | Recommended | Optional | Not applicable |
| Static frontend / docs site | Optional | Optional | Optional | Not applicable |
| Batch job (GP-002) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** if using autonomous pipeline |
| Infrastructure-only repo (Terraform) | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** | **Required** (infra generation) |

**`.ai/context.yaml`** — machine-readable declaration of the Golden Path, compliance scope, team, and catalog version pin. For HIPAA-scoped services, PHI fields must be enumerated here. PHI field enumeration is required before AI agent use is authorized on a HIPAA repository (PTN-APP-GOV-002, Compliance Requirements).

**`.ai/constraints.md`** — prohibited patterns and mandatory controls derived from the Verification Contract and AI Governance Policy. This file is loaded by AI agents to constrain generation. Keep it to the most critical rules — agents with overloaded constraint files produce lower-quality output (PTN-APP-GOV-002, Best Practices).

**`.ai/instructions.md`** — Tool-agnostic agent instruction file. Summarizes the active Golden Path ID, the three most critical constraints, and the catalog URL in plain prose consumable by any AI agent (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Code Assist, autonomous pipelines). Pre-populated by the scaffold; sourced from PTN-APP-GOV-002. Tool-specific bridge files (e.g. `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) are optional thin wrappers that point to this file if the tool does not read it natively.

**`.ai/catalog-ref.yaml`** — required for repositories where an autonomous pipeline generates code without human session initiation. Contains the catalog API endpoint, pinned version, and fetch behavior for the pipeline's catalog loader.

**For existing repositories:** Use the platform migration script to generate context files from the repository's `service.yaml` declaration rather than hand-authoring them (PTN-APP-GOV-002, Phase 2 Step 3):

```bash
platform-tools generate-ai-context --from service.yaml --output .ai/
```

Review the generated files. PHI field declarations require security architect sign-off before AI agent use is authorized.

### Step 1.3 — Register the Repository with the Platform Developer Portal

Update the Platform Developer Portal to include this repository as an adopter of its declared Golden Path. This registration enables:
- Automated deprecation notices when the path is deprecated (PTN-GOV-AI-001)
- Automated catalog version update PRs when a new path version is released (PTN-APP-GOV-002, Example 3)
- Adoption count tracking used in quarterly catalog reviews (PTN-GOV-AI-001)

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#phase-2-warning-only-pilot]

## Phase 2: Warning-Only Pilot

Before the conformance gate and fitness suite are set to fail-hard mode for a repository, run them in warning-only (`warn`) mode for a minimum of **2–4 weeks** (PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001). This is not optional; it exists to protect teams from false positives that would block legitimate work.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#what-warning-only-mode-does]

### What Warning-Only Mode Does

The gate runs all checks. Violations are reported in the conformance report and surfaced in the pipeline output. The **pipeline does not halt**. Teams can ship work while reviewing and remediating violations.

Warning-only mode is **a temporary transition state, not a permanent configuration** (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001). It must have a defined target date for promotion to fail-hard. Setting warning-only mode with no target date is equivalent to publishing no governance at all.

Set the target fail-hard date before deploying in warning-only mode. Communicate this date to the team.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#what-to-do-during-the-warning-only-period]

### What to Do During the Warning-Only Period

1. Review every warning in the conformance report on each pipeline run.
2. Classify each warning:
   - **Genuine violation**: Team needs to fix a real gap. Add it to the sprint backlog.
   - **False positive**: The rule is triggering incorrectly on a valid configuration. Document it and raise a ticket with Platform Engineering.
3. Track the **false positive rate**. The target threshold for promoting to fail-hard mode is **< 1% false positive rate** (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, Phase 2 Step 4).
4. Fix genuine violations during the warning-only period. The goal is to reach a state where the gate would pass in fail-hard mode before you flip the switch.

Do not promote to fail-hard mode until false positives are below the threshold. A fail-hard gate with a high false positive rate will generate exception tickets for violations that should not exist — wasting triage time and eroding trust in the gate.

---
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#phase-3-fail-hard-activation]

## Phase 3: Fail-Hard Activation

Activate fail-hard mode only when:

- [ ] Warning-only period has run for ≥ 2 weeks
- [ ] False positive rate is < 1%
- [ ] The exception management process is published (GUID-GOV-PROC-002)
- [ ] ARB triage SLA is in place (1 business day)
- [ ] Platform Developer Portal documentation is updated with the gate behavior and exception process for this path (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, Phase 3 Step 1)
- [ ] Team has been informed of the go-live date and what to do if the gate fails

Update the gate configuration in the CI/CD pipeline to `mode: fail` (or `mode: deny` for the policy gate):

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
- name: Architecture Conformance Gate
  uses: gainwell/actions/conformance-gate@v1
  with:
    catalog_url: ${{ vars.GOLDEN_PATH_CATALOG_URL }}
    mode: fail          # was: warn
    evidence_store_url: ${{ vars.EVIDENCE_STORE_URL }}
    exception_tracker_url: ${{ vars.JIRA_API_URL }}
```

**After going live**, monitor the exception ticket rate for the first 2 weeks. A spike in exception tickets after fail-hard activation indicates either genuine gaps the team missed during warning-only mode (team resolves) or false positives not caught during the pilot (Platform Engineering resolves by updating rules).
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#pipeline-stage-order]

### Pipeline Stage Order

The full verification pipeline runs in this order (PTN-APP-GOV-001):

```
Conformance Gate → Build → Fitness Suite → Policy Gate → Deploy
```

- **Conformance Gate** (Layer 1): Structural checks against the Verification Contract. Runs first. If it fails, the build does not run (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001).
- **Architecture Fitness Suite** (Layer 2–3): Behavioral and runtime-configuration checks. Runs after build, before the policy gate. Fail-hard after the warning-only pilot (PTN-APP-GOV-001).
- **Policy Gate** (Layer 3): Infrastructure policy evaluation against Terraform plans or Kubernetes manifests. Runs before deploy (PTN-INFRA-GOV-002).
- **Deploy**: Runs only if all gates pass.

New fitness functions for a Golden Path are introduced in warn-only mode for one release cycle before graduating to fail-hard, allowing teams time to remediate (PTN-APP-GOV-001, Graduated enforcement).

---
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#phase-4-post-deployment-monitoring-activation-layer-4]

## Phase 4: Post-Deployment Monitoring Activation (Layer 4)

Pre-deployment gates verify the system at the time of deployment. They cannot detect behavioral drift that occurs after deployment: configuration changes applied outside the pipeline, emergent violations from combinations of valid individual changes, or runtime state that diverges from declared configuration.

Runtime invariant monitors provide continuous post-deployment verification (PTN-APP-GOV-003). For Golden Paths with HIPAA or FedRAMP scope, Layer 4 monitoring is part of the compliance assurance chain.

**You do not need to manually configure the monitors.** The `invariant-monitor-provisioner` pipeline step reads the declared Golden Path from `service.yaml` and activates the monitors defined in the path's Verification Contract automatically on the first deployment. The team receives a notification within 15 minutes of the first successful deployment confirming which invariants are being monitored.

Layer 4 monitors are only activated when Layers 1–3 (conformance gate, fitness suite, policy gate) are already running in fail-hard mode. Activating runtime monitoring before pre-deployment verification is enforced provides false assurance (PTN-APP-GOV-003, Prerequisites).

---

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#catalog-version-updates]

### Catalog Version Updates

When a new Golden Path version is published, all repositories on the previous version receive an automated PR from the `catalog-version-updater` GitHub Action (PTN-APP-GOV-002, Example 3). The PR:
- Bumps `catalog_version` in `.ai/context.yaml`
- Updates the pinned version in `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml`
- Includes a description of the breaking changes in the new version

Review the PR description. If the new version introduces breaking changes (see the path changelog in the Developer Portal), assess the impact before merging. If the new version introduced a new required fitness function check that your service does not yet satisfy, the check will run in warn-only mode for one release cycle before graduating to fail-hard (PTN-APP-GOV-001).

If the bumped catalog version introduces a new required Verification Contract check and your service cannot meet it, file an exception per GUID-GOV-PROC-002 rather than leaving the automated PR unmerged indefinitely. An unmerged catalog update PR means your AI context is pinned to an older version that may contain obsolete constraints.

**Target currency:** Keep catalog version lag to **< 2 minor versions behind current** (PTN-APP-GOV-002, Monitoring and Metrics).
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#path-deprecation]

### Path Deprecation

When a Golden Path is deprecated, every repository declaring that path receives an automated GitHub issue (PTN-GOV-AI-001, Example 3). The issue includes:
- The retirement date (90 days from deprecation date)
- The superseding path ID
- A link to the migration guide
- An estimated migration effort

**The 90-day window starts on the deprecation date, not when you read the issue.** Check `#platform-engineering` Slack or the Developer Portal for path deprecation announcements.

Standard migration steps (PTN-GOV-AI-001, Example 3):
1. Review the migration guide linked in the GitHub issue
2. Update `service.yaml` → `golden_path: [new-path-id]`
3. Update `.ai/context.yaml` → new catalog URL and catalog version
4. Run the migration tool: `platform-tools migrate-path --from [old-id] --to [new-id]`
5. Verify the conformance gate passes on the next pipeline run
6. Close the GitHub issue

**After the retirement date:** The old path is removed from the machine-readable catalog index. The conformance gate reports `unknown-path` for repositories still declaring the retired path. If you cannot complete migration within the 90-day window, contact Platform Engineering before the window closes — not after (PTN-GOV-AI-001).

---
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#optional-autonomous-generation-path]

## Optional: Autonomous Generation Path

For teams using the intent-to-infrastructure autonomous pipeline (PTN-TEC-AI-001), the `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml` file and the `Catalog Fetcher` pipeline step replace manual context loading. The pipeline fetches the live Golden Path specification at generation time.

**Pre-enabling autonomous deployment**, run the pipeline in **generation-only mode for 4–6 weeks**: the pipeline generates code and infrastructure but waits for a human merge before deploying. During this soak period, measure the **first-pass verification success rate** — the percentage of generations that pass all three pre-deployment gates without manual code changes. A success rate below 80% indicates that the intent document schema or the context files need improvement before autonomous deployment is appropriate (PTN-TEC-AI-001).

Multi-environment soak windows for autonomous deployments (PTN-TEC-AI-001):
- **Dev**: Gate passes → auto-merge
- **Staging**: 24-hour soak window before promotion
- **Production**: Mandatory human gate — no autonomous promotion to production

### What Do I Do When the Gate Fails?

See [GUID-GOV-PROC-002 Exception Management Process](GUID-GOV-PROC-002-exception-management-process.md), specifically the Exception Lifecycle section.

Short version: read the conformance report, fix configuration gaps, only file an exception if you have a genuine technical constraint that prevents you from conforming to the rule.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#can-i-use-a-path-in-experimental-status]

### Can I Use a Path in `experimental` Status?

A path in `experimental` status has not completed full ARB review. You can pilot it as a team, but:
- It cannot be used as an AI agent generation target (PTN-GOV-AI-001)
- Fitness suite checks on `experimental` paths run in warn-only mode only
- Do not build production infrastructure on an `experimental` path

A path moves from `experimental` to `active` after full ARB review. Until then, treat it as a preview.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#which-review-track-applies-to-my-change]

### Which Review Track Applies to My Change?

From PTN-GOV-AI-001, Governance Decision Guide:

| Event | Review Track | Approver | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| New Golden Path (first publication) | Full ARB review | ARB | 2-week cycle |
| Security CVE patch to bundled dependency | Express review | CISO sign-off | 48 hours |
| New optional component (non-breaking) | Platform Engineering review | Platform Engineering Lead | 1 week |
| Breaking change — MAJOR version bump | Full ARB review + migration plan | ARB | 2-week cycle |
| Experimental path promotion to `active` | Full ARB review | ARB | 2-week cycle |
| Deprecation initiation | ARB notification + 90-day notice | ARB notification | 90-day window |
| Exception to a path requirement | ARB exception review | ARB | 2-week cycle |

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#example-1-new-hipaa-microservice-from-scaffold]

### Example 1: New HIPAA Microservice from Scaffold

A team on benefits-platform creates a new eligibility API using the GP-001 scaffold generator. The scaffold generates the full directory structure, service.yaml, `.ai/` context files (including `.ai/instructions.md`), and the base CI/CD pipeline template. The team adds business logic. On the first pipeline run, the conformance gate runs in warn-only mode (Platform Engineering configured this as the default for new repositories). It reports two warning-level violations: an OpenAPI spec file is missing, and the `healthz` endpoint returns HTTP 503 on startup delay.

The team fixes both during the first sprint. At week 3, the gate is promoted to fail-hard mode. It passes on the first run. The policy gate (Terraform plan evaluation) also passes. Layer 4 runtime monitors activate on the first production deployment. The team receives a confirmation notification within 15 minutes.
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#example-2-existing-service-adopting-a-path-retroactively]

### Example 2: Existing Service Adopting a Path Retroactively

A team adopting GP-001 for an existing service they have been running for two years uses the migration script to generate `.ai/` context files from `service.yaml`. The service has 38 structural differences from the GP-001 scaffold. The team runs the conformance gate in warn-only mode for 4 weeks while addressing violations sprint-by-sprint.

At week 4, 33 of 38 violations are resolved. 5 remain: they require changes to how the service manages secrets that will take another sprint to safely implement. The team confirms with Platform Engineering that the false positive rate is 0% (none of the remaining violations are false positives — they are genuine gaps). They set the fail-hard date to the end of the next sprint when the secret management changes will be complete. Gate goes live on schedule with a clean pass.
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#example-3-catalog-version-update-with-a-breaking-check]

### Example 3: Catalog Version Update with a Breaking Check

GP-001 is bumped to v1.3.0. The automated PR from `catalog-version-updater` arrives in 18 repositories. The PR description notes one new required Verification Contract check: `OBS-003` — trace context must be injected in all outbound HTTP calls. Twelve teams merge the PR. Their services already inject trace context. Six services open exception requests: they use a service mesh that handles trace injection transparently at the infrastructure layer — their services do inject traces but not in the code layer the check looks for.

Platform Engineering evaluates the six exceptions together. Rather than approving six individual exceptions, Platform Engineering adds a contract exemption for service-mesh-managed trace injection to the Verification Contract v1.3.0 (PTN-GOV-AI-003, Scenario 3). All six exceptions are closed. This outcome is normal functioning of the exception process — the batch of exceptions is the signal that the check needs a known-good alternative.

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

- **HIPAA-scoped services**: PHI fields must be declared in `.ai/context.yaml` before AI agent use is authorized (PTN-APP-GOV-002). The conformance gate and all three layers of pre-deployment verification are mandatory.
- **FedRAMP-scoped services**: All context files plus `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml` are required. Full gate stack required.
- **Context file currency**: Catalog version declared in `context.yaml` must be recorded in pull request metadata for AI-assisted or AI-generated commits (PTN-APP-GOV-002, Compliance Requirements).

[strategy/guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-003-golden-path-adoption-playbook.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog coverage — new workloads using an approved path | ≥ 80% within 12 months of path publication | Conformance gate telemetry |
| Exception rate per path | < 10% | Exception tracking registry |
| Context file coverage — AI-enabled repositories | 100% within 6 months | Repository metadata scan |
| Context file currency — catalog version lag | < 2 minor versions behind current | Automated catalog version check |
| Conformance gate pass rate for paths in fail-hard mode | ≥ 97% | Gate report aggregation |
| Path freshness — paths with no review in > 12 months | 0 | Quarterly catalog review |

## TL;DR

```
Before you start: verify all prerequisites are in place (catalog, Verification Contract, Evidence Store, exception process).

Per repository:
  1. Add golden_path to service.yaml
  2. Create .ai/ context files (use decision guide for which are required)
  3. PHI fields required in context.yaml before AI use on HIPAA services
  4. Run conformance gate + fitness suite in warn-only mode for 2–4 weeks
  5. False positive rate must be < 1% before promoting to fail-hard
  6. Exception process must be published before fail-hard goes live
  7. After first deployment, Layer 4 runtime monitors activate automatically

Ongoing:
  - Merge catalog version update PRs promptly (catalog-version-updater opens these)
  - Deprecation notices: 90-day window, fix or contact Platform Engineering before it closes
  - Keep catalog version lag < 2 minor versions
  - Exception rate > 10% for a path → path needs updating, not team discipline
```
